reviews.review:
Zcrew is a mixed bag for me. There are times I feel Zcrew is trying to be some kind of Helldivers mixed with zombies. The problem is it never even comes close to the fun of that game. 

The characters, environments, and on screen action graphics are good, and the sound of the weapons have actually been one of the standout highlights in my opinion. 

As an online co-op, I couldn't tell you anything about it ... because there is NO ONE playing! Well, there is one playing it. It would be nice to try it out though since I can tell it would benefit from a team. You can tell it was intended for co-op by some of the battles you have to take on from all sides. 

Gameplay in the solo realm has been somewhat fun but lacking. I don't have a problem with character movement. Seems a tad bit slippery, and i do mean a tad, but still works just fine. There are times you wonder if it will ever pick up the pace, and then you get bombarded by mutated monstrosities that take everything you can throw at them. 

Interface decisions are one of the biggest head scratchers for me. For some reason, the dev team decided to make it really up close third person while in your headquarters area for a game that is an isometric twin-stick shooter. It look nice, but feels odd and clunky. It becomes difficult trying to figure out what to do, as well. The mission menus are anything but intuitive. Also, you apparently have to upgrade in one area and wander around to discover you must incorporate them to your character in another area. They should stay full top-down isometric and do away with this awkward third person area. 

I am currently working to level up and unlock abilities and make new weapon purchases. 

I know this is an early release and I was willing to give to the cause of what I am hoping is a hardworking new dev team. I am going to put some more time in and re-edit this review if things change in the future. The mixed bag is that I want this to be good, but it isn't yet. I am currently marking thumbs down until I can see improvements. However, it is good enough to support for the money being asked for in early access. You can tell much time has gone into it so far.
